questions.q: Which chart of accounts segment carries LTV's balancing values, and what are those values?
questions.explain: The Company segment is the balancing segment, with 1000 representing the US parent and 2000 the Canadian subsidiary.

questions.q: Which three cost center values exist in both LTV entities?
questions.explain: Assembly (410), Fabrication (420), and Corporate Overhead (510) are the three cost centers configured for both the US and Canadian entities.

questions.q: What is account 7850, and why is it flagged in this lesson?
options: Accounts Payable — Trade, and it's a long-standing account
Freight Out — Customer Shipments, a new account that matters again later in the capstone
Cash — Operating, assigned only to the Canadian entity
Accumulated Depreciation, used only for fixed assets
questions.explain: Account 7850, Freight Out — Customer Shipments, is explicitly called out as a new account that resurfaces as part of Chapter 3's investigation.

questions.q: What values are allowed in the Intercompany segment, and what restricts them?
options: Any natural account value, with no restriction
Values mirroring the Company segment, restricted so an entity can't name itself as its own intercompany partner
Only the value 0000, reserved and unused
Values matching the Cost Center segment
questions.explain: The Intercompany segment mirrors the Company segment's values (1000, 2000), with a cross-validation rule preventing an entity from using its own value as its intercompany partner.

questions.q: Why does this lesson emphasize that Period 1, Jan-26, is significant?
options: It's the last period before the fiscal year changes
It's a leap-year period requiring special calendar handling
It is this configuration's first-ever month-end close, with no prior closing history
It's the only period assigned to the Canadian ledger
questions.explain: Period 1, Jan-26, is this brand-new configuration's very first month-end close — directly setting up Chapter 3's January 31 crisis.
